claims.text: CuMoTaWV films are refractory high-entropy-alloy coatings.
Magnetron-sputtered CuMoTaWV films typically have a nanocrystalline grain structure.
Deposition parameters and post-deposition heat treatments can tune CuMoTaWV grain sizes from approximately 10 to 50 nm.
The near-surface grain-size distribution and associated grain-boundary characteristics govern wear performance.
An intermediate grain size of approximately 20–30 nm maximizes beneficial grain-boundary-mediated sliding.
An intermediate grain size of approximately 20–30 nm promotes self-lubrication.
Very fine grains near 10 nm may cause superplastic deformation and structural instability.
Coarse grains near 50 nm reduce grain-boundary density.
Reduced grain-boundary density in coarse-grained films increases friction and wear.
Wear performance has a non-monotonic dependence on grain size over approximately 10–50 nm.
Films with grain sizes of approximately 20–30 nm will have lower friction coefficients than films with grain sizes near 10 or 50 nm.
Films with grain sizes of approximately 20–30 nm will have lower wear rates than films with grain sizes near 10 or 50 nm.
The proposed grain-size relationship applies to refractory HEA coatings under similar deposition, heat-treatment, environmental, load, and sliding conditions.
Significant compositional heterogeneity or grain sizes outside 10–50 nm may produce different wear behavior.
Established grain-size effects on mechanical behavior provide prior support for the hypothesis.
Annealing may introduce microstructural changes other than grain growth that interfere with the proposed grain-size effect.

contradictions.description: The intervention says grain size will be tuned through controlled changes to deposition parameters and heat treatment, whereas the conditions state that all films are produced under identical sputtering conditions. It is therefore unclear whether deposition parameters vary or are held constant.
